verdicts.summary: The note's only hazard is that the code-fallback link is absent until a call succeeds. That is finding 0. The 'stuck relay session' spinner is the unverified part of the note.

The note's failure mode is a non-owner on the tunnel host being sent to the hosted page with no way back to the code page. That is finding 0. I found no extra hazard: a crafted peer-link link still goes through approve(), which only blocks the pairing-code branch for peer-link clients.
I tried a renewal that outlasts the 10 s outer timeout and a decision POST that times out. Neither strands the user, so the ~40 s bound holds.
verdicts.scenario: Token renewal inside the request loop takes longer than 10 s, so the outer timeoutOrElse fires. The renewal runs in a fiber forked into the service scope, so it is not cancelled. It caches the new token, and the user's retry reuses it. The exchange has its own 30 s cap (DPOP_AUTHORIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS). A timed-out decision POST may already have been applied, but the retry only mints another single-use code. The cost is a misleading error message (see finding 1). A session id that changes on renewal is finding 2.

verdicts.summary: I tried to find a redirect the server could issue that agentRedirectUrl would block. There is none, because the server accepts only a subset of what the client allows.
verdicts.scenario: A legitimate agent redirect uses http://localhost, http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1] with any port, or any https URL. Registration accepts only those (parseRedirect). The client check accepts https and any http loopback host, including [::1], so it is at least as permissive and never blocks a registered URI. javascript: and data: URLs cannot pass registration and are refused client-side.

verdicts.summary: I tried to get Approve submitted during the 700 ms disarmed window (Enter in the form, a click right after focus). Both are blocked.
verdicts.scenario: Right after load or a focus/visibility event, `armed` is false. The Approve button is disabled, and the form's onSubmit calls decide only when canApprove is true, so Enter in the code field does nothing. Deny is intentionally not gated. decide() does not check `armed` itself, but its only approve caller is the gated submit handler. After a failed decision `armed` stays true.

verdicts.summary: I tried the open question: a managed policy that keeps remote clients out but the hosted approval path still being used. It cannot happen, because such a policy leaves the tunnel hostname empty.
verdicts.scenario: Under a policy without remote clients, allowsConnect is false. server.ts then never installs the cloudflared connector, so connector.hostname is null and CloudLink.linkState sends no tunnelHostname. hostedApprovalUrl needs state.tunnelHostname to equal the issuer host, so it returns none and the agent stays on the environment's own page. EnvironmentAuth.ts:1446 also disallows Connect-paired sessions under that policy. The wizard's missing-code dead end when the server falls back is finding 7. The lost Access-step policy message is finding 6, but the policy itself is not bypassed.

verdicts.summary: I tried a defect, a timeout, or a missing relay session making the hosted page's load or decision never resolve (a permanent spinner). Every non-success is converted to a failed Result, so the page always gets an answer.
verdicts.scenario: runConnectMcpApproval returns Result.fail(squashAtomCommandFailure(result)) for any non-Success outcome, including defects such as session pending, and the surface renders an error message. A typed failure gives 'Could not reach that environment…' and a defect gives 'Could not reach this environment. Try again.' The signer is read with serviceOption, the same way other callers do it. CORS allows the authorization and dpop headers for the cross-origin call. The misleading wording is finding 1.
